candidates.title: Cresswell model: 0* is not the only world where p is false, and the truth-set analysis of p is wrong
candidates.quote: 付値は $p$ が $0^{\ast}$ でだけ偽とする。
candidates.problem: The definition says p is false only at 0*. But the proof of logic:cresswell-finite-cofinite uses `[p]=W\setminus\{0^{\ast}\}` (p true everywhere except 0*), which contradicts the definition. More seriously, the whole Magari argument depends on the valuation. With p false only at 0*, check the Cresswell model: at 1*, the successors are 0* (since 1≤0+1) and all of N; p is false at 0*, so 1* ⊭ □p. At 2*, successors are n* with 2≤n+1, i.e. n≥1, plus all of N; p is true at all of these (0* excluded), so 2* ⊨ □p. Then 2* ⊭ □□p since 2*R1* and 1* ⊭ □p. So the counterexample to 4 still works. But the claim in the proof of logic:cresswell-validates-h Case 1 that `n から見えるのは n より小さい自然数だけ` is fine. The real problem: the lemma logic:cresswell-finite-cofinite states `[p]=W\setminus\{0^{\ast}\}` which is the opposite of the definition. This is an internal inconsistency: either the definition or the lemma is wrong. If p is false only at 0*, then [p] = W \ {0*}, which is cofinite — consistent with the lemma's conclusion but the lemma's displayed equality is then correct only under the reading 'p is false only at 0*'. Actually [p]=W\{0*} IS correct under the definition. So no error there. Re-examine: the definition and the lemma agree. Drop.
candidates.defense: The definition and the lemma agree: p false only at 0* gives [p]=W\{0*}. No error.

second_opinion.reason: The reported problem itself retracts its claim: under the definition 'p is false only at 0*', the truth set is [p] = W \ {0*}, which is exactly what the lemma logic:cresswell-finite-cofinite states. So the definition and the lemma agree, and there is no inconsistency. The reporter's own re-examination confirms this, and the Magari counterexample (2* ⊨ □p, 1* ⊭ □p) works as written. No concrete error remains.

candidates.title: Magari: claim that 2* ⊨ □p requires checking all successors including 0*
candidates.quote: $2^{\ast}Rx\iff x\neq0^{\ast}$（$2\le n+1\iff n\ge1$、および $\N$ の元すべて）なので $2^{\ast}\models\Box p$。
candidates.problem: 2*R0* holds since 2≤0+1 is false — wait, 2≤1 is false, so 2*R0* does NOT hold. The condition is m≤n+1 with m=2, n=0: 2≤1 false. So 0* is not a successor of 2*. Good, the parenthetical is correct. And p is false only at 0*, so all successors of 2* satisfy p. Correct.
candidates.defense: 2≤n+1 iff n≥1, so 0* is excluded; p is true at all other worlds. Correct.

second_opinion.reason: The quoted sentence is correct as written: in the Cresswell model, 2* sees exactly the worlds x with x ≠ 0* (among N* this is n ≥ 1 since 2 ≤ n+1 iff n ≥ 1, and 2* sees all of N), so since p is false only at 0*, every successor of 2* satisfies p, giving 2* ⊨ □p. The reporter's own analysis confirms this (2 ≤ 0+1 is false, so 0* is not a successor of 2*), and the subsequent step 2*R1*, 1*R0*, 0* ⊭ p correctly shows 2* ⊭ □□p. There is no error; the report itself concludes 'none' for a fix.

candidates.title: Lewis's theorem Step 3: the induction claim and the role of B
candidates.quote: $\mathcal{A}$ の元（その $\Box$ の中身は $\mathcal{A}\subset\mathcal{B}$）について帰納法を回すと、$\mathcal{B}$ の元と $\Box\mathcal{B}$ の組み合わせすべてで $[G]=\lvert G\rvert$。
candidates.problem: Step 3 claims [G]=|G| for G built from B∈B and □B (B∈B) by ⊥,→. The induction is on A's subformulas; but the class of G includes □B for arbitrary B∈B, and B itself may contain □ of subformulas of A. The induction needs to establish [B]=|B| for all B∈B simultaneously with [□B]=|□B|. The text says 'induction on elements of A' but the □B case is proved assuming [B]=|B| for B∈B, which is a stronger induction hypothesis than 'for elements of A'. Since B is built from A-elements by ⊥,→, [B]=|B| follows from [E]=|E| for E∈A by the ⊥,→ clauses. So the induction is: first [E]=|E| for E∈A (atomic and Boolean, with □E handled using [E']=|E'| for E'∈A), then [B]=|B| for B∈B by Boolean composition, then [□B]=|□B|. This is a nested induction and is routine. No gap.
candidates.defense: The induction is a standard two-level induction; the text indicates it. Routine.

second_opinion.reason: The reported problem itself concludes 'No gap' and proposes no fix; it argues the induction is routine and the text is correct. Re-reading Step 3 confirms this: the lemma is proved by induction on the construction of G, with the □B case explicitly assuming [B]=|B| for B∈B, and the final sentence about induction on elements of A is just a summary remark, not a load-bearing claim. candidates.title: Problem solution: deriving Löb from H⊕4 — step (i) uses distribution to get C→(□□p→□p)
candidates.quote: (i) 分配公理より $C\to(\Box\Box p\to\Box p)$、公理 4 と合わせて $C\to(\Box p\leftrightarrow\Box\Box p)$。

Axiom 4 gives C→□C (since C is □(...), 4 gives □(...)→□□(...)=□C). So C→□(□p↔□□p). Correct. (iii) Henkin with A=□p: □(□p↔□(□p))→□(□p), i.e. □(□p↔□□p)→□□p. Correct. Then (ii),(iii) give C→□□p, and (i) gives C→(□□p→□p), so C→□p. Correct.
